answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The knoll multiplier is published, charged in ember, and voyage lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3882 identities would post 4152 proofs and burn roughly 53 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
